Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum for the POC:

Recap:
- Use case: secure clinical note summarization for internal triage (PHI in input).
- Key asks: whether Redwood can sign a BAA, which deployment options are eligible for PHI, and how PHI is handled (logs, caching, key management).

Short answers up front:
- BAA: Redwood can execute a BAA for customers using Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted API we have limited BAA options on a case-by-case basis — generally we recommend Dedicated or Private for PHI.
- PHI boundaries: PHI should not be stored in shared caches or long-term logs for PHI workloads. Redwood provides options to disable logging, enable prefix/KV cache controls, and use customer-managed encryption keys in Dedicated/Private.
- SOC 2 / GDPR: Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report and baseline GDPR controls; SOC 2 report is available under NDA.

Next steps we propose:
1) I will send our HIPAA overview and the vendor security questionnaire you can start filling out (attached).
2) Technical deep-dive with Dev (sales engineer) and Evelyn (security) to walk through PHI boundaries, key management (KMS/HSM), and deployment architecture (30–45 min).
3) Procurement/Docs: If procurement wants an estimated cost and draft BAA, loop in Tom and procurement so we can surface Dedicated sizing and commercial template.

Attachments: Redwood-HIPAA-Overview.pdf, MedCare-Vendor-Security-Questionnaire.xlsx

If that plan looks good I'll get the calendar invites out — suggested time windows for the tech call: Mon/Tue next week between 10–2 PT.

Hi Sarah — thanks for the questions, answered inline below.

1) Hosted API retention: by default, Redwood does not retain request or response payloads for analytics in a way that is accessible to other customers. For PHI-sensitive workloads we can (a) disable request/response logging for your account, (b) prevent telemetry ingestion for content, and (c) configure a shorter retention window. That said, our recommended, supported path for PHI at scale is Dedicated or Private, where telemetry and logs can be fully controlled per-customer.

2) VPC/private mode: yes — our Private deployment is designed so customer workloads run in your VPC or on-prem, with optional customer-managed KMS. In Private mode PHI payloads never traverse Redwood shared control plane storage; network and key controls are customer-managed. Dedicated also offers strong isolation (dedicated GPU pools) and support for customer-managed keys; it is commonly used for PHI with a BAA.

3) BAA eligibility: Redwood will sign a BAA for Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted API we evaluate case-by-case and often require additional contractual controls; if procurement needs a definitive answer for the POC we can surface a commercial note but expect Dedicated/Private to be the recommended path.

Additional notes (security): Evelyn (cc'd) — we can provide the SOC 2 Type II report under NDA, the typical encryption-at-rest/in-transit details, and a short architecture diagram showing where PHI may be cached (KV cache) and how to disable that.

Suggested immediate next steps:
- Tom/procurement: if you can start the questionnaire we attached, we'll review and flag any gaps.
- Dev/Evelyn: I'll propose two time slots for a technical call early next week.

Happy to discuss cost estimates for Dedicated sizing once we have expected QPS/sequence lengths.

Best,
